high.title: Minyakita Cooking Oil Smells Like Diesel Fuel, Producer Faces Heavy Sanctions
high.summary: Minyakita, the government-subsidized cooking oil brand, was found to smell like diesel fuel in Central Java, affecting recipients of food aid in Karanganyar, Klaten, and Wonogiri districts. The Ministry of Trade has ordered an immediate recall and replacement of the affected products while an investigation is underway to identify the root cause. This incident raises serious food safety and supply chain integrity concerns for the government's subsidized commodity program.

high.title: Tokopedia's Future After Wave of Layoffs: GOTO Confirms No Material Financial Impact
high.summary: Publicly listed PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia (GOTO), which holds a 24.99% stake in Tokopedia, has officially stated that the recent round of layoffs at Tokopedia will have no material impact on its share of net profit or on e-commerce service fee revenues. ByteDance (TikTok's parent) holds the majority 75.01% stake in Tokopedia. The disclosure, filed with the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI), is significant for GOTO investors monitoring the financial health and restructuring of the Tokopedia entity.

high.title: Government Launches 3 Economic Stimulus Packages to Protect Public Purchasing Power
high.summary: The Indonesian government has launched a series of economic stimulus packages for the second half of 2026, aimed at sustaining public purchasing power amid global challenges. Measures include a 30% discount on train and Pelni sea transport fares during school holidays and the Christmas-New Year period, port service fee waivers for ferry transportation, and VAT borne by the government (PPN DTP) for air transport. These stimulus measures are significant for investors as they signal active government intervention to support domestic consumption and create multiplier effects across the transportation and retail sectors.

high.title: Ministry of Agriculture Allocates IDR 1.33 Trillion to Transform Papua Selatan into a Food Barn
high.summary: Minister of Agriculture Andi Amran Sulaiman has disbursed IDR 1.33 trillion in agricultural aid to Papua Selatan Province as part of a strategic push to establish the region as a key food production hub in eastern Indonesia. The funding covers land development, irrigation, agricultural machinery, seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and crop modernization programs under the Cetak Sawah Rakyat (CSR) and Land Optimization (Oplah) initiatives. This large-scale investment is relevant for investors in the agribusiness and food security sectors, as it signals significant government commitment to boosting domestic food production and reducing dependency on imports.

high.title: Tokopedia's Fate After Being Hit by Mass Layoff Storm
high.summary: GOTO (GoTo Gojek Tokopedia), which holds 24.99% of Tokopedia shares, confirmed there will be no material impact on net profit following Tokopedia's massive layoffs of approximately 90% of its workforce after TikTok's parent ByteDance took majority control with 75.01% ownership. GOTO also assured that e-commerce service fees received from Tokopedia will remain unaffected. This is a significant corporate event for GOTO shareholders and Indonesia's e-commerce landscape.

high.title: GOTO Speaks Out on Tokopedia's Mass Layoffs, Holds 24.99% Stake
high.summary: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia (GOTO) responded to reports of Tokopedia cutting approximately 90% of its employees following TikTok's takeover, describing the move as part of an organizational restructuring strategy. GOTO, holding a 24.99% stake, stated it respects management decisions made by Tokopedia's new leadership under ByteDance. This development is highly relevant for GOTO investors on the IDX as it signals major structural changes in Indonesia's leading e-commerce platform.

high.title: GoTo Announces Share Buyback of IDR 3.5 Trillion
high.summary: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) has announced a share buyback program worth up to IDR 3.5 trillion, pending approval at an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPSLB) on June 18-19, 2026. The buyback will be executed over a 12-month period from June 19, 2026 to June 18, 2027. This is a significant corporate action for one of Indonesia's largest tech companies, signaling management confidence in the company's valuation and potentially supporting the GOTO share price.

medium.title: Government Communications Agency Defends Appointment of Diverse-Background Commissioners to State-Owned Enterprises
medium.summary: The Head of the State Communication Agency (Bakom), Muhammad Qodari, defended the government's practice of appointing commissioners from diverse, non-industry backgrounds to state-owned enterprises (BUMN), arguing it brings fresh perspectives to support the government's agenda. The appointments have drawn public scrutiny, with critics questioning the suitability of some nominees. This issue is relevant to investors in BUMN-listed companies as board composition can influence corporate governance quality.

medium.title: Gold Prices Rise Rp 25,000 Per Gram Over the Past Week, Now at This Level
medium.summary: Antam gold prices rose 0.94% over the past week, gaining Rp 25,000 per gram to close at Rp 2,670,000 per gram on July 4, 2026, after dipping to Rp 2,625,000 mid-week before recovering strongly from Thursday onward. The weekly price movement reflects continued investor interest in gold as a safe-haven asset in Indonesia. This is relevant to retail investors and those tracking commodity price trends in the local market.

medium.title: List of Top 10 Countries Whose Citizens Rode the Whoosh High-Speed Train in Indonesia
medium.summary: The Indonesia-China High Speed Railway (KCIC) carried 184,740 foreign passengers in the first half of 2026, with Malaysian nationals being the largest user group at 74,902 passengers. Since launching in October 2023, the Whoosh train has cumulatively served 866,458 foreign passengers on the Jakarta-Bandung corridor. Growing foreign ridership supports the commercial viability and tourism contribution of the high-speed rail infrastructure investment.

medium.title: Over 1 Million People Benefit from Ferry Fare Discount Program
medium.summary: The government's ferry fare discount program has reached 90.04% of its target, with 1,086,400 passengers and vehicles benefiting out of the 1,206,585 targeted, during the school holiday period from June 20 to July 5, 2026. Beneficiaries include 907,409 passengers in 341,210 vehicles and 178,991 walk-on passengers. The strong uptake demonstrates effective execution of the government's transportation stimulus and reflects healthy domestic mobility demand, relevant to investors tracking consumer activity and transportation sector performance.

medium.title: Government Communications Agency Responds to Controversy Over SOE Commissioner Appointments
medium.summary: The Head of the Government Communications Agency (Bakom), Muhammad Qodari, has defended the appointment of commissioners with diverse, non-industry-specific backgrounds at state-owned enterprises (SOEs/BUMN), arguing that varied perspectives help align companies with the government's broader agenda. Qodari cited his own experience as an SOE commissioner without a matching industry background as an example of how outside viewpoints can generate alternative solutions. This is relevant for investors in Indonesian SOEs as commissioner composition can influence corporate governance, strategic direction, and overall confidence in state-owned enterprise management.

medium.title: Foreign Tourists Quietly Embrace Train Travel in Indonesia, Data Reveals Growing Trend
medium.summary: PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) reported serving 308,874 foreign tourists in the first half of 2026, a 2.54% increase compared to 301,219 in the same period of 2025, signaling growing international appeal for rail travel in Indonesia. KAI attributes the trend to the unique travel experience offered by trains, including scenic views of rice fields, mountains, rivers, and heritage areas. This growth is a positive indicator for KAI's revenue diversification and the broader Indonesian tourism and transportation sectors.

Indonesia's Ministry of Trade has ordered an immediate recall and replacement of the affected products while an investigation is underway to identify the root cause. Producers involved face the threat of heavy sanctions, raising concerns over food safety and supply chain integrity for the subsidized cooking oil program.

medium.title: Gold Price Rises Rp 25,000 Per Gram Over the Week — Current Price Here
medium.summary: Antam gold prices rose 0.94% over the past week, climbing from Rp 2,645,000 per gram on Monday June 29 to Rp 2,670,000 per gram by Saturday July 4, a gain of Rp 25,000 per gram. Prices initially dipped to Rp 2,625,000 mid-week before recovering strongly from Thursday onward. This weekly performance is relevant for Indonesian retail investors and those tracking safe-haven asset trends.
